hints: For coplanar forces in equilibrium, the sum of resolved components along two perpendicular directions must each equal zero.
Resolve along the horizontal and vertical axes to obtain: $F + 2F\cos 45^\circ = 30\sin\theta$ and $2F\sin 45^\circ + 3F = 30\cos\theta$.
Divide the two equations to eliminate $F$ and solve for $\tan\theta$, then find $\theta$.
Substitute the value of $\theta$ back into either equation to calculate the magnitude $F$.
walkthrough:
State the fundamental condition for a system of coplanar forces in equilibrium: the resultant force in any two perpendicular directions must be zero:
$$\sum F_x = 0,\quad \sum F_y = 0$$

Set up horizontal equilibrium. The force $F$ acts horizontally to the left, the force $2F$ acts at $45^\circ$ above the horizontal to the left, and the force $30\text{ N}$ acts at an angle $\theta$ to the vertical, giving a rightward horizontal component of $30\sin\theta$:
$$F + 2F\cos 45^\circ = 30\sin\theta$$
Factor out $F$ on the left side:
$$F(1 + 2\cos 45^\circ) = 30\sin\theta\quad \text{(Equation 1)}$$

Set up vertical equilibrium. The force $3F$ acts vertically downwards, the vertical component of $2F$ acts downwards as $2F\sin 45^\circ$, and the force $30\text{ N}$ has an upward component of $30\cos\theta$:
$$3F + 2F\sin 45^\circ = 30\cos\theta$$
Factor out $F$ on the left side:
$$F(3 + 2\sin 45^\circ) = 30\cos\theta\quad \text{(Equation 2)}$$

To eliminate the unknown $F$, divide Equation 1 by Equation 2:
$$\frac{30\sin\theta}{30\cos\theta} = \frac{F(1 + 2\cos 45^\circ)}{F(3 + 2\sin 45^\circ)}$$
$$\tan\theta = \frac{1 + 2\cos 45^\circ}{3 + 2\sin 45^\circ}$$

Substitute $\cos 45^\circ = \sin 45^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ so that $2\cos 45^\circ = \sqrt{2}$:
$$\tan\theta = \frac{1 + \sqrt{2}}{3 + \sqrt{2}}$$
Evaluate the numerator and denominator:
$$1 + \sqrt{2} \approx 2.414214,\quad 3 + \sqrt{2} \approx 4.414214$$
$$\tan\theta = \frac{2.414214}{4.414214} \approx 0.546918$$
$$\theta = \tan^{-1}(0.546918) \approx 28.7^\circ\quad (28.675^\circ)$$

Now substitute $\theta = 28.675^\circ$ into Equation 1 to find $F$:
$$F(1 + \sqrt{2}) = 30\sin(28.675^\circ)$$
$$F(2.414214) = 30 \times 0.479867 = 14.3960$$
Divide both sides by $2.414214$:
$$F = \frac{14.3960}{2.414214} \approx 5.96\text{ N}$$
